reviews.decision: The lifecycle adapter keeps runtime initialization, external ownership, and process-exit finalization together; collectives, packet operations, and ghost requests are split into separate native units.
The ghost adapter combines platform guards with request validation and cancellation so MPI request lifetime is closed in one native boundary; transport orchestration remains outside the file.

The top-level build file is the intentional composition root for the library, optional backends, examples, and tests; its dependency count is tracked without splitting target ownership into opaque fragments.
The C ABI fixture keeps one end-to-end lifecycle scenario so ABI ordering and cleanup remain visible; its length is registered for review rather than hidden from the repository report.
The bounded-view fixture validates related invalid-input cases in one contract scenario; its length is tracked and remains outside production code.
The contract fixture groups the public and internal invariant checks needed to detect drift across the SDK boundary; the review signal remains explicit.
The dynamics fixture keeps deterministic physical cases together so shared setup and comparison rules cannot diverge; the signal is registered for later focused decomposition.
The hierarchy fixture compares tree construction and solver behavior in one deterministic scenario; its test-only function length is visible and reviewed.
The lifecycle fixture intentionally exercises construction, mutation, failure, and cleanup in sequence; the signal is accepted as a test-harness responsibility review.

MPI qualification is kept in one process-aware harness so rank setup, scenario selection, parity, migration, rollback, and overlap modes share one communication contract; all three signals remain tracked.

The architecture gate keeps one five-argument file-analysis boundary so profile thresholds and exception handling are applied consistently; the signal is registered and does not waive production thresholds.
The callable scanner handles C++ lexical edge cases and explicit exceptions in one validator; its branching is tool-local and remains covered by its fixture suite.
The formatter implements the repository's scope-sensitive grouping grammar and recursive statement handling; the current complexity is exposed for a later tool decomposition instead of ignored.
The frozen-plan gate validates mutually dependent manifest, roots, phase, CTest, naming, and forbidden-reference contracts; its signal is registered while the gate remains a single policy boundary.

The naming report materializes separate collision, exception, length, and type-mapping result lists so CI can distinguish each contract failure; the allocation signal is limited to report construction.

The public boundary gate keeps include, pointer, fixed-width ABI, internal-facade, and parameter-exception checks in one diagnostic boundary so a public contract violation reports its owning rule and source line.
